title: The Red Ball
text: A boy called Tim has a red ball. He takes it to the park. His dog comes with him. The dog runs after a bird. The ball goes under the big oak tree. Tim looks for the ball. He looks and he looks. Then he sees a hole near the tree. Tim puts his hand into the hole. The ball is in the hole. He takes the ball out. He kicks the ball to the dog. The dog is happy now. Tim is happy too. His mother waits at the gate. The sun is warm today.

title: The Box on the Bus
text: A girl called Ana is on a bus. She has a blue box in her hands. The box is for her new shoes. The bus is late because of the rain. Ana looks at her bag. The shoes are not in the bag. The box is empty. She is sad. Then she looks under the seat. The shoes are under the seat. Ana takes them out. She puts them in the box. She smiles at the window. The rain stops and the sun comes out. She is late for school today.

title: The Raincoat on the Chair
text: Tom was playing in the yard, and the sky became dark. His mother called him in because the rain was coming. He ran to the door and put his boots on. His boots were left by the door. While he was looking for his raincoat, the water came in through the open door. The raincoat was still on the chair in the hall. It was wet, so Tom asked his sister for a towel. His sister was reading a book. She gave him the towel and closed the window. Then they sat down and looked at the rain. The rain was loud on the roof.

title: The Bike That Would Not Stop
text: Ben wanted to ride his new bike to the park, but the chain made a loud noise. He got off and looked at the chain. The chain was loose, so he asked his father for help. His father showed him how to fix it. Although the repair took a long time, Ben did not want to give up. If he fixed the chain, he could go to the park before it got dark. The noise stopped, and Ben rode home very fast. He put the tools back in the box and left the box in the shed. The sun was low over the trees, and the sky was orange.

title: The School Garden
text: The school garden was empty for two years, because the old trees had fallen and nobody planted anything new. A new class asked their teacher whether they could grow food there, although several children thought it would be too hard. The teacher said that if they worked together, they could start with beans and tomatoes, since these plants do not need much water. So they cleared the ground, and although the work was tiring, they finished it in three weeks. Because they took turns every day, the garden stayed alive. By the end of the term, they had picked more vegetables than the school could eat, so they gave half of them to the families.

title: What a Seed Needs
text: A seed is a part of a plant. It has a hard coat. The coat keeps the seed safe. A seed needs three things. It needs water. It needs air. It needs warm soil. Then the seed begins to grow. A small root goes down into the soil. The plant grows up to the sun. The plant will grow bigger every day. Some seeds sleep for many months. They wait for the cold to pass. Then the warm rain wakes them up. Every seed has a small plant inside it. That plant is waiting to grow.

title: How Bread Is Made
text: People make bread from flour, and flour comes from wheat. A farmer cuts the wheat in a field. He takes it to a machine. The machine turns the wheat into flour. A baker mixes the flour with water, salt and yeast. Yeast is a small living thing. It eats the sugar in the flour and makes gas. The gas makes holes in the dough. After the baker shapes the dough, the hot oven bakes it. The bread comes out brown, and it smells good. The baker sells it in the morning.

title: Where Rain Comes From
text: Rain comes from the sea. The sea gets its water from rivers and from the ground. The sun is warm, so it pulls the water up into the air. This water is called water vapour. While the vapour rises, it becomes cold, and the cold water turns back into tiny drops. Millions of these drops together make a cloud. The cloud is heavy, so the drops fall down as rain. When the rain reaches the ground, it runs into the rivers again. The whole journey starts once more. The water is always on the move.

title: The Parts of a Bicycle
text: A bicycle is a machine with many parts, and each part has a job. The frame holds the rider and the other parts together, but it does not move by itself. The two wheels roll on the ground. The chain joins the pedals to the back wheel, so when the rider pushes the pedals, the wheel turns. The brakes slow the bike down when the rider squeezes the handles. Although the parts are simple, they must work together, because a bike with a loose chain will not move. A good rider checks the tyres and the chain before every ride.

title: Paper and Trees
text: Paper is a thin sheet that people make from wood, and almost all the paper in the world comes from trees. A large tree is cut down, and its trunk is sent to a factory. There the wood is broken into pieces and mixed with water. This soft mixture is called pulp. The pulp is spread on a moving belt, and water is pressed out of it. A hot roller dries the sheet. The sheet is pressed again until it is smooth and strong. Although one tree gives only a little paper, a forest can supply a great deal. If people plant new trees and use paper carefully, the raw material will not run out.

title: What Is in the Bag?
text: A girl has a bag. Her friend comes to play. 'Hello,' says the girl. 'What is in your bag?' asks the friend. 'I do not know,' says the girl. Then she looks in the bag. 'It is a cat!' she says. The cat says nothing. 'Is it your cat?' asks the friend. 'Yes, it is,' says the girl. Then they play with the cat. 'Look at the cat,' says the girl. 'It is black and white.' 'My father gave it to me last week.' 'He said I must feed it every day.' 'Now I am afraid it will run away.' 'Come in,' says the girl. 'You can hold it. Be careful.'

title: The Wet Shoes
text: 'Where are my shoes?' asks Mei. She looks under the bed. 'They are not here,' she says. 'They were here, because I put them by the door this morning.' Her brother comes into the room. 'Maybe the dog took them,' he says. Mei looks at the dog. The dog looks at the floor. 'Look,' says Mei. 'The dog has one shoe in his mouth.' 'Now we know where the shoes are!' Then she takes the shoe away and puts the shoes on. Mei puts her shoes on and goes out.

title: The New Student
text: 'Is this seat free?' asks a boy. It is the first day of term. 'Yes, you can sit here,' says Ana. The new boy puts his bag on the floor. 'My name is Peter,' he says. 'My name is Ana,' she says. 'I have a new book about trains.' 'Can I see it?' asks Peter. 'Yes. You must be quiet in the reading room,' says Ana. 'I will be,' says Peter. While the teacher writes on the board, the two children look at the book together. They do not say a word.

title: The Swimming Lesson
text: 'I do not want to go in,' says Tom. He stands by the side of the pool. 'The water is cold, because it is morning,' says the coach. 'But the sun is coming out,' says Tom. 'If you put your foot in, it will feel better,' says the coach. Tom puts one foot in the cold water. 'That was not so bad,' he says. Although he still did not want to jump, he counts to three and jumps in. The water is cold, but soon his body feels warm. 'That was the best thing I did today,' he tells his mother that evening.

title: The Last Train Home
text: 'We will miss the last train,' says Rui. The rain is heavier now, and the station is far away. 'If we run, we get wet, but if we wait, we miss it,' says his sister. 'Then we should ask the driver,' says Rui. They wave down a bus, although the driver is in a hurry. 'The station is closed,' he says, 'but I can take you to the next one.' At the next station, because the train is late, they have time for hot tea. When the train comes, Rui says they would be wet and cold if they had run. They are warm, and the train arrives as they sit down.
